newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on technicals, demand.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on technicals, demand.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures touched the lower $10.00 per ton limit but closed just off the lows on Friday on ideas high prices had rationed demand, traders said.
Soyoil also ended lower, shrugging off Friday's USDA Supply and Demand report which showed a 15-million bushel cut in soybean ending stocks to 125 million bushels.

Traders focused instead on ideas demand was faltering and pointed to the National Oilseed Processors Association weekly crush of 25.94 million bushels. That figure was the lowest since October 10, and came in below trade expectations for 26.32 to 27.2 million bushels.

"This report is based on March 1 conditions," a trader said. "It's April 11. We've seen a significant reduction in the crush in the last three weeks, you've had reduction of demand from Taiwan and Europe because of (hog) disease."

The trader was referring to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan that was expected to cut deeply into Taiwan's feed imports. A swine fever epidemic in the Netherlands was also seen cutting into Europe's feed usage.
Soymeal ended $9.70 to $0.50 per ton lower with May down $9.20 at $274.80. Soyoil closed 0.44 to 0.30 cent per lb lower with May off 0.38 at 23.84.
Chartists said the market responded to technical indicators that had been giving off bearish signals since last Friday's limit losses.

The May soymeal contract was showing technical weakness after it failed to pierce a key chart point at $290.60 per ton. Long liquidation overwhelmed input from USDA's report after the market failed to reach that level, traders said.
Some trade sources said a head and shoulders formation in the May and July pointed to more losses.

Floor sources reported massive long liquidation. Funds sold at least 1,200 lots of soymeal and commercials were also said to be on the sell-side. Cargill Inc alone sold at least 1,200 lots of soymeal, pit sources said.
Refco Inc sold 400 lots July and 200 May, Merrill Lynch sold 400 July and Griffin Trading sold 300 May and 100 July.
In soyoil, Cargill bought 1,200 lots July and 200 May but sold 600 July, traders said. Prudential Securities sold 300 July and CIS sold 200 May and 100 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 25,000 lots, compared with Thursday's actual volume 20,859 lots. Soyoil was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Thursday's 14,861.
